rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies an equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy compared with pure tungsten, while the hidden target designed a non-equimolar Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 alloy within the Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W system and compared it with equimolar NbMoTaVW. The hypothesis uses a different alloy system and a different baseline, so it is a different kind of intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses room-temperature uniaxial compression, but with different specimen geometry, strain rate, and additional indentation and scratch tests, whereas the target used only room-temperature quasi-static compression on different specimen dimensions and a different strain rate, plus hardness and nanoindentation. The conditions share only the broad room-temperature compression regime.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: Both invoke reduced valence-electron concentration to promote plasticity, but the hypothesis adds solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and grain-boundary cohesion mechanisms, while the target focuses on VEC-driven shear instability and Peierls–Nabarro barrier reduction. The general class of VEC-mediated ductility is shared, but the specific pathways and structural mediators differ.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher strength and greater plastic strain relative to pure tungsten, while the target predicts greatly improved ductility with only a limited sacrifice in strength relative to equimolar NbMoTaVW. Both predict improved plasticity, but the property direction is compared against different baselines and the hypothesis includes additional outcomes (fracture toughness, BDTT) not measured in the target.
